what: The Round 16 build of F71-F75 was cut off by 'Command aborted' during one long scripted batch of model CLI edits, which left unsaved edits (PaymentMode enum, payNow operation, PaymentGatewayInfo and PaymentEventInput TOs) in the CLI dirty file. None of F71-F75 was built.
why: A single long chained CLI script with no checkpoint was aborted; the dirty model file survived the abort.
workaround: judo-cli discard --force; model status returned to base match with no unsaved changes; scratch files r16-a.sh and zz-probe.spec.ts deleted.

what: At the start of the build the app was down: the probe spec got ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on localhost:8181. judo.sh status reported Keycloak not running and its image missing, so the builder had to docker start the Postgres container, run judo.sh start in the background and sleep 140 s.
why: The stack was stopped between rounds; judo.sh status gives no restart recipe and Keycloak image state is not explained.
workaround: docker start postgres-webshop; nohup ./judo.sh start; sleep 140; curl check returned 200.

what: kb_get on agent-docs/backend/custom-operations.agent.md with section 'Rules for Custom Operations' returned not found, although kb_search had returned that exact path and heading one call earlier. The builder then read the companion from disk.
why: Index refresh was still running at the time of the search ('results may be stale'), or the section lookup does not match the companion heading. The file exists on disk.
workaround: Read catalog/agent-docs/backend/custom-operations.agent.md from disk (lines 265-272 of custom-operations.md read directly).

what: kb_get on best-practices/model/token-based-verification-workflow.md with section 'Public entry points need an anonymous actor' returned not found, though kb_search had returned that path and heading as hit 1. The file exists on disk.
why: Same stale-index window as c11-03, or the section lookup failed on a heading containing a hyphenated word.
workaround: kb_search on anonymous actor, then grep of the file from bash.

what: kb_get on best-practices/backend/generator-ignore-config-protection.md with section 'Practice' returned not found; kb_search later returned the same path, so it is not a missing file.
why: Section name 'Practice' did not resolve; the file exists on disk.
workaround: Retried through kb_search and kb_get on another path; the file itself was not read in this chunk.

what: kb_get on best-practices/frontend/i18n-generator-override-extra-fragment.md with section 'Practice' returned not found, though kb_search returned the path (hit 1). The same path without a section worked two calls later.
why: Section lookup by the name 'Practice' fails for this file; a path-only fetch works.
workaround: Fetched the path without a section (L6272) and read the file from disk with read tool (L6275).

what: kb_get on best-practices/frontend/generator-ignore-i18n-layout.md with section 'Practice' returned not found. The path is referenced by a wiki link in the Hungarian page and was never a kb_search hit; the file exists on disk.
why: Section lookup failed on a path that was only reached through a link, not a search hit.
workaround: Gave up on that section; relied on hungarian-full-localization.md instead.

what: kb_get on agent-docs/backend/README.md with section '.generator-ignore - One Rule' returned not found, although kb_search had listed that heading for this path. The One Rule text the builder needed came back from agent-docs/frontend/README.agent.md, which is a different file.
why: The path/heading pair from the search hit does not resolve; the same wording exists in the frontend README.
workaround: kb_get on agent-docs/frontend/README.agent.md with the 'Understanding .generator-ignore > One Rule' section worked (L6249).

what: kb_get on agent-docs/e2e-testing/README.md with section 'E2E Testing Guide > Key Concepts > Best Practices' returned not found, although kb_search had returned it at hit 3 with the same parent heading.
why: Section lookup failed for a nested heading path in a README.
workaround: Grep of the README from bash (L6343) for the Best Practices list.

what: kb_get on agent-docs/integration-testing/best-practices.agent.md with the heading path 'best-practices.md - index > Best Practices > 5. Logging and Debugging > 6. Test Isolation' returned not found. kb_search showed '6. Test Isolation' nested under 'best-practices.md - index > Best Practices > 5. Logging and Debugging', so the path given was wrong.
why: Heading path not as indexed; numbered headings in the breadcrumb make the chain hard to build from a search hit.
workaround: Read the Test Isolation section from disk with grep (L6343).

what: kb_get on agent-docs/frontend/build-and-deployment.md with section 'Frontend Build and Deployment > Maven Build Modes > Checksum Handling' returned not found; kb_search had returned the same file as hit 3 with the heading 'Checksum Handling'.
why: Full breadcrumb path with a '>' chain did not resolve; the shorter heading would have worked (not tested).
workaround: grep of the file from bash for 'checksum' (L6333).

what: The kb guard fired repeatedly ('3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base', 'Repeated source searching, still no kb consult') on bash/ctx_execute greps of catalog files that had been used because kb_get failed. About nine warnings in the chunk.
why: The guard counts disk reads of catalog files as source searches; kb_get misses (c11-03 to c11-11) pushed the builder to disk reads, which then triggered the guard.
workaround: Kept running kb_search after each warning; continued reading catalog files from disk (about 14 times in this chunk, e.g. L6110, L6112, L6137, L6275, L6283, L6290, L6313, L6349).

what: kb_search for schema-upgrade and SCHEMA_DIR did not surface the schema_dir setting. The GAPS entry R12-1 still says schema_dir is not in the kb. A later grep of the catalog found it in schema-evolution.agent.md line 27 only; build-process.md's schema-upgrade row (line 299) and its note (line 306) do not mention schema_dir.
why: The setting is documented only in the agent companion of schema-evolution; the build-process page that kb returns for schema-upgrade omits it.
workaround: Used schema_dir from the catalog grep; did not use schema-upgrade for the data-keeping migration.

what: The judo CLI query --select rejected a nested selection (principal{fqn}) with 'not a field of ActorType', while the same field works inside a GraphQL query. Earlier, query --select fqn,principal failed with 'Subselection required' for a transfer-object field.
why: The CLI --select syntax does not accept object sub-selections; the error text does not say so.
workaround: Used judo graphql with an explicit selection set instead (L6299).

what: judo CLI query --where accepted only KEY=VALUE pairs; the operator form fqn~DashboardInfo was rejected with a format error.
why: The CLI supports equality only; the error gives the format but not the list of supported operators.
workaround: Used grep on the full query output instead.

what: judo CLI update --schema=<Type> returned 'not a field' for type names (ActorType, Operation) and listed the valid fields of the element, while create --schema=ActorType worked. The meaning of --schema differs between update and create.
why: The --schema option behaves differently per command; update expects a field of the element, not a type name.
workaround: Used the create form and the query command to read the metamodel.

what: Both actor types (Customer and Admin) are stored with anonymous=true. The builder's review says the catalog defines anonymous as a guest that is open to anyone, yet unauthenticated POSTs return 401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, so the flag does not make the actor public at runtime as the catalog implies.
why: The catalog text (accesspoint rules) and the observed runtime behaviour disagree; the reviewer could not reconcile them from the catalog alone.
workaround: Recorded as review item R16-R3 and catalog item C3 in REVIEW-R16.md; no model change (review round).

what: The catalog contradicts itself on whether identifier flags are enforced: the composite-identifier practice says the agent-docs do not state how the flag is enforced, while structure.md line 75 says the runtime enforces it. The reviewer raised this as catalog item C4.
why: Two catalog pages describe the same flag with different claims.
workaround: Logged in REVIEW-R16.md as C4; webshop business keys (GiftCard.code, Invitation.inviteKey, Quote.number) were not flagged as identifiers (review R16-R11).

what: The catalog says application_hu-HU.json is generated from the model and must be listed in .generator-ignore. The webshop's make-hu-translations.py docstring says a new locale file is not a generated file and needs no ignore entry, and the file has survived 15 rounds of generation with no entry.
why: The generator only emits application_en-US.json for a one-language model; the Hungarian file is a hand-made locale, so the catalog text is wrong for this case.
workaround: Kept scripts/make-hu-translations.py as the source of the Hungarian file; no .generator-ignore entry.

what: The singleton page says whether and when the platform calls an initializer operation is not documented. The builder's seed for the ShopConfig row (R10-4) therefore has no documented startup hook.
why: The catalog does not describe a startup hook for initializers; the reference-data page also leaves it open.
workaround: scripts/seed-dev-user.sh and a manual seed; ShopConfig seed still open.

what: Keycloak self sign-up has no model setting. The catalog's multi-tenant realm page says the exported realm does not set registrationAllowed, and the only documented route is the Java RealmManager. The seed script PUTs the realm with registrationAllowed=true instead.
why: The realm is emitted by asm2keycloak with loginWithEmailAllowed only; no model attribute exposes registrationAllowed.
workaround: scripts/seed-dev-user.sh PUTs the realm after each fresh Keycloak volume (R7-4 still open).

what: The generated integration-test module pom declares hu.blackbelt.osgi.i18n:i18n-api with an empty version element, so the module cannot build. kb search for the integration-test module did not return this, and the catalog does not document the empty version.
why: Generator output defect in the integration-test module; the documented route (mvn in application/integration-test) does not work for this project.
workaround: Hand-written order-tests module (carried from R12-5); the generated pom is not edited.

what: The generated Playwright config sets retries: 4 unconditionally; the catalog note in playwright.ci.config.ts recommends the conditional form (retries only in CI). The builder's review notes the default config is parallel with 4 retries.
why: Generated default differs from the catalog's recommended form.
workaround: Used playwright.local.config.ts with workers 1 and retries 0 (L6339).

what: Review item R16-R21: E2E specs share and pollute seed data. The default Playwright config is parallel with retries, but the specs only work with one worker; the catalog's test-isolation rule (truncateTables default true) is for backend tests, and the e2e best practice only asks for TEST_DATA_PREFIX.
why: Specs were written for a serial run and rely on shared rows; the catalog e2e practice (prefix test data, clean up) was not applied to the webshop specs.
workaround: Logged for later; no change in review round.

what: The interceptor page says getInstance() identifies the instance with its old values, while getInput() carries the new values. The builder's audit interceptor re-reads the old row through the DAO, so the page does not say whether the instance payload is reliable for old values.
why: The one-line description is ambiguous about which fields the instance payload holds.
workaround: ProductAuditInterceptor reads the old product through productDao.getById before compare.

what: The Quartz page says the platform provides no scheduler and that the docs do not describe the transaction or variable context of a plain scheduler thread. The builder needs that context for the F73 release job.
why: The catalog gives no transaction or ACTOR variable model for threads outside a request.
workaround: Planned to manage UserTransaction inside each job, per the Quartz practice; F73 not built in this round.

what: Review item R16-R2: checkout writes the whole product row, so a mask does not limit what is written. The catalog says the mask only shapes the read-back and does not limit writes, so the checkout code (or its mask use) is wrong. A concurrent checkout fails with 'no records updated' and surfaces as a 500, not NOT_ENOUGH_STOCK.
why: Builder used a full update where the catalog says the write set is whatever the payload carries; the optimistic-lock failure is not mapped to a modeled fault.
workaround: Recorded as review item R16-R2 (bug) for the next build round; no change in review round.

what: Review item R16-R1: the header cart counter goes stale after a cart line or coupon is removed. The cart code uses 'webshop:cart-changed' in registerCartHooks.ts and Cart.tsx, while CartButton and shopEvents.ts listen on 'shop:cart-changed'. The catalog says event keys are internal and not to be relied on; the documented route is the post-operation refresh handler.
why: Two hand-written event names; the custom code bypassed the documented post-refresh hook for the remove path.
workaround: Recorded as bug R16-R1; no change in review round.

what: Review item R16-R5: ProductAuditInterceptor writes audit rows in preCall and catches RuntimeException (line 79) and continues. On PostgreSQL a failed insert aborts the whole transaction, so the update fails later with a confusing error, and the catalog's note on caught DAO exceptions is not followed.
why: Interceptor swallows the exception; the catalog says a caught DAO exception does not roll back by itself and PostgreSQL aborts the transaction after a failed statement.
workaround: Recorded as risk R16-R5; no change in review round.

what: Review item R16-R14: every build in this project runs with judo.sh build -i (and generate -i), so the checksum guard that would show hand-edited generated files is off. The builder could not say whether any generated file is patched.
why: Repeated use of -i to get past the R9-13 checksum failure, which was never root-caused.
workaround: Recorded as deviation R16-R14; no change in review round.

what: Before the Round 16 model change the builder copied the old RDBMS model (base5-rdbms_postgresql.model) and ran pg_dump to dump-before-r16.sql (8.3 MB) so that the existing data could be migrated, not wiped.
why: schema-upgrade applies generate and execute in one step, so no hand-written backfill can be inserted; the documented route is generate, backfill, then execute.

what: The review round (no code changes) discarded the unsaved model edits left by the aborted build with judo-cli discard --force, rather than saving them, so that the model matched e35dddd.
why: The review round forbids model or code changes; the dirty edits were partial and unreviewed.

what: Customer rows are provisioned by a hand-written CustomerProvisioningInterceptor on the first customer-client login, and Admin rows are not created automatically. The reason given is the catalog's gotcha that the runtime does lookup only, not first-login insert.
why: The access-point and authentication pages state that managed/claim actors are looked up and a missing row raises AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND; the interceptor must insert the row.

what: Review item R16-R13: any customer can create gift cards worth up to the maximum for free and spend them (the buy path has no payment step). The gift card code generator uses SecureRandom correctly, but the buy operation issues the card at once.
why: The F-function was built as a stand-in for payment; the catalog's payment and external-API adapter pattern was not yet in use.
workaround: Recorded as risk R16-R13 for the payment round (F71).

what: Review item C9: the injectable-clock recipe in the catalog says LocalDateTime.now follows the JVM time zone and Timestamp!now follows defaultZoneId, but the builder's review says the recipe uses systemDefaultZone, which clashes with the platform zone.
why: The clock recipe mixes two zone sources; the review cites a clash the catalog text does not state in this chunk.
workaround: Recorded as catalog item C9 in REVIEW-R16.md; not re-verified against the recipe code in this chunk.

what: A sed -i call on macOS failed because BSD sed needs an empty suffix argument; the rerun with sed -i '' worked.
why: GNU sed syntax used on a macOS host.
workaround: Re-ran with sed -i ''.

what: The builder guessed the PostgreSQL table name T_ENTITIES_WEBSHOP_SALESORDER, which does not exist; the real table is t_webshop_sales_order, found with information_schema.
why: Guessed table name without checking the generated naming for this project.
workaround: Queried information_schema.tables.
